steps.name: Museum PA
steps.text: Please queue here for tickets... Please queue here for tickets to the 'Encounter with a Resurrected General from the Time of the Shah' special exhibition!

steps.name: Museum PA
steps.text: Please queue here for tickets, please queue here for tickets...

steps.name: Fervent Crowd
steps.text: Yes, eyes on me, look at me, not the camera.

steps.name: Fervent Crowd
steps.text: Please wait just a moment! I need to straighten my bridal gown!

steps.name: Fervent Crowd
steps.text: I worked all night to make this, but I guarantee with my three thousand tales about the Shah that it is historically accurate!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Please note flash photography is prohibited in this exhibition, to prevent damaging the cultural artifacts.

steps.name: Fervent Crowd
steps.text: Alright! Lets do twenty burst shots!

steps.name: Visitor On Hoverboard
steps.text: Hey guys, I'm finally inside the most mysterious room of the Varjavandabad Museum.

steps.name: Visitor On Hoverboard
steps.text: Now, I'm going to smoothly record the movements of this heroic general from all angles and uncover the secrets of the resurrection in the City of Radiance.

steps.name: Young Visitor
steps.text: Dad, its legs look empty inside.

steps.name: Young Visitor
steps.text: You hear that, Dad? It sounds like it's empty inside when I knock on it!

steps.name: Visitor On Phonecall
steps.text: Mhm, yes, this batch of goods must be delivered to Higashi. It's not a large order, but we can't come off as unreliable...

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Sir, please look after your child.

steps.name: Visitor On Phonecall
steps.text: Sorry, hold on, I'm a little busy... Hey! Come back here! Don't run off touching everything!

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Please don't make noise in the museum...

steps.name: Visitor On Phonecall
steps.text: Hey, you're the ones who decided to pull off this open exhibition and even let your exhibit wander around! You didn't even limit the number of visitors, so it's no wonder the place is so rowdy!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Acting Curator Anat believes that 'History and knowledge should be made equally available to all', and thus she has not established a tiered ticketing system.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Also, the sixty centimeter-high guardrails around my display are meant to prevent visitors from intruding into my space. If your child crosses the rails, you will be flouting the rules and regulations of this place.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Please cooperate with the staff...

steps.name: Tourist With Coins
steps.text: Gah! I missed!

steps.name: Tourist Reading Guide
steps.text: This guide doesn't say which currencies work.

steps.name: Tourist Reading Guide
steps.text: To be fair, the guide doesn't even say if tossing a coin will bring good luck.

steps.name: Tourist With Coins
steps.text: Why not try it anyway, just in case?

steps.name: Tourist Reading Guide
steps.text: ...Give me a coin. I should aim for its torso, right?

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Please... stop... this is an important historical artifact...!

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: There's too many of them, I can't handle them all...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Understood. I will use my weapon to slice the incoming projectiles apart.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: (Lifts hand)

steps.name: Visitor in Armor
steps.text: Arrgh—!

steps.name: Visitor in Armor
steps.text: Everyone, look!

steps.name: Visitor in Armor
steps.text: I'm role-playing a Nightzmoran warrior from a thousand years ago! Ack, I have been defeated! What a grand historical re-enactment!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: My weapon did not make any contact with his body.

steps.name: Visitor in Armor
steps.text: Oh, General of the Shah! A few words for your defeated foe, perhaps!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Back in my day, the most common phrase one would hear in the army when beheading captured enemy leaders was 'The insects shall devour your entrails'.

steps.name: Visitor in Armor
steps.text: Okay, sure, if you could just say that again...

steps.name: Visitor in Armor
steps.text: Hey, hey! Don't come over while I'm still lying on the ground! You're gonna cause a stampede!

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Oh no... I should call for backup.

steps.name: Museum Staff
steps.text: Who could've guessed there would be so many people here to see a walking mummy when the Flood Festival is going on?

steps.name: Woman of High Status
steps.text: Hatshepsut Hanimefendi, I hear you've been spending recent days looking for a particular gem lately.

steps.name: Woman of High Status
steps.text: It just so happens my family is in possession of one, so I've brought it here for you. I hope it can alleviate your worries.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Thank you so, so much... please let me see it...

steps.name: Woman of High Status
steps.text: I wonder if I might be fortunate enough to host you at my home for dinner sometime soon?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: So sorry, hanimefendi, but I've been crazy busy lately.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Thank you for taking the trouble to bring me the gem, but I'm sorry to say it's not the one I'm looking for.

steps.name: Woman of High Status
steps.text: Oh, truly a pity. I will bother you no more, Hatshepsut Hanimefendi. Until we meet again.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Uh... how many more do we still have outside?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Seventy-three, and they all claim to have the gem you're looking for.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Why are there so many?!

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Just tough it out and take a break at noon. Some gemstone merchants from the Grand Bazaar say they've found some clues, so we'll go over then to take a look.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: You call that a break...?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Of course. You'll only be seeing gemstones, no people.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Ah...

steps.name: Gem Merchant
steps.text: Anat Hanim, the Padishah's daughter has been sitting here frowning for the past three hours. Are you still interested in the remaining gemstones?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: How many do we have left?

steps.name: Gem Merchant
steps.text: More than two hundred...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: ...Leave them here, we'll finish looking through this crate first.

steps.name: Gem Merchant
steps.text: Very well, I'll take my leave then.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Anat... did someone come by earlier?

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: They delivered another crate of gemstones.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Anat, something's wrong... why does your head look like a prism...?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: The furnishings too... they're sparkling...

steps.name: Anat
steps.text: Pepe!!!

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: The museum has finally opened its doors?

steps.name: Museum Receptionist
steps.text: Yes, Aspasia Hanim. The special exhibition tickets are in high demand! I heard wind of it last night and wanted to tell you to queue up early, but I couldn't find you.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: It's alright, that's not what I'm here to see. It's the collector I'm looking for.

steps.name: Museum Receptionist
steps.text: You seem to be in a good mood.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: As I thought, language is a bridge to peace, communication serves as a foundation of understanding, and this historic city is also abundant with knowledge.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: *sigh* Sargonians have been proud of their glorious history since antiquity. How wonderful it would be if they were willing to sit down for a long conversation, instead of plundering everywhere they go.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: That collector understood how persistent we Minoans could be, after my explanation, and I also gained much from his insights into the city...

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Right, there is something I want to ask you.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: In modern Menat-Ha'mait, are silver crafts more valuable than those made from gold?

steps.name: Museum Receptionist
steps.text: Haha, are you joking?

steps.name: Museum Receptionist
steps.text: Of course, it does happen from time to time... for example, under pain of death by a lord ameer.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...I see, thank you for the clarification.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: May I ask if that companion of mine has returned?

steps.name: Museum Receptionist
steps.text: Yes, with two other friends as well.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Two other... friends?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Very well. The more heads to share ideas with, the better. I'd love to find more Kurantas as passionate and frank as she.
Aspasia walks up the hotel stairs and stops before the door.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Narantuya, are you in there?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I bring good news. That collector who won third place has decided to return my goblet to me after listening to my three-hour speech!

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Would you like to come with me to the museum to look at both goblets together...?

steps.name: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.text: ...I didn't see anyone go in or out of that room with the gemstone last night, Narantuya.

steps.name: Unfamiliar Voice
steps.text: I was hiding on the roof of the opposite building with my eyes peeled the entire time.

steps.name: Narantuya's Voice
steps.text: ...You know how important this kidnapping is. This is the only way to quickly get a big pile of money.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: I'm sorry, Narantuya. We'll go look for the Padishah's daughter right away.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It's too late for that.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: The caravan I got to be our cover is about to leave the city. Even if we manage to find and snatch her, we won't have a way out.

steps.name: Ajani
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Let's focus on what to do next.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Both of you should go back to the museum, but avoid contact with the girl. Report in as soon as you find any other way to make money.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I'll go look for the lost gemstone and return it to Aspasia. That's the least I can do...

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: You don't have to do that.
Ajazi suddenly feels a deadly silence descend upon the room.
She looks at the intruding stranger, shifts her gaze to Narantuya, and finally turns her head to Ajani with eyes pleading for help.
Ajani raises a finger to her lips with her other hand inching towards the sedative at her waist.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Uh, I can explain, Aspasia.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: We were just mapping out our plan. Once it's done, I'll return you your gem, or something of equal value. You can trust me on that.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Oh, and, these are my other two subordinates...

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: What plan?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I heard you planning to bait the Padishah's daughter with that gem, in order to kidnap her.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...You heard everything?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: My apologies, I had no intention of eavesdropping on your conversation. I just happened to be standing by the door.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I believe communication lays the foundation of understanding, but I also know you have a large debt to pay and need money urgently.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: So, would you like to tell me the whole story?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: To be honest, I don't have a clue where the gem is right now. There's nothing I could ask you to do, even if you want to help.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: The past is in the past, and our plan now... Well, we basically don't have one.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: You know that's not what I'm talking about.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: If I tell you why I owe this debt and need the money, will you help me?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I believe we can discuss a more honest and conscientious way to do it.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Heh, I knew you'd say something like that.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Aspasia, mind holding your hand out for me?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: What for?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: For old times' sake... I just want to...
Ajani and Ajazi exchange looks with each other.
They are certain Narantuya's call to action is the moment when they hear the crisp clacking of her heels on the ground.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ——Ask you for a discount on what I owe you.

steps.name: Ajazi and Ajani
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I've been staying with you for weeks and even took your gem. I have to pay you back for all that.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: This coin purse holds one thousand and two hundred dinars. I know it's not enough, but... I mean, we're such good friends, aren't we?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Narantuya...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Ah, there's a bunch of foreign coins in there too. Some merchants might not recognize them, but I'm sure you'll find somewhere to spend them.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Here's some gemstones too. They're tiny and impure, but they make up for it in number.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: So... could you be a bit flexible with my debt?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...Narantuya!

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Are you so unwilling to have an actual discussion about this with me?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: 'Communication lays the foundation of understanding', right? I already get you, though.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Maybe you spent day after day in your temple copying statues to work out the basics of swordsmanship, or maybe you followed your parents and took an oath passed down through generations.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: More importantly, you're one of the innumerable followers of the Minoan heroes, so I'm sure your soul is pure.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You'd definitely help out someone about to fall from a tall building, and you'd speak up to anyone who used more... exceptional methods.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Yes, you're right.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I believe a scale of good and evil lies within all our hearts, and one exists within the laws of the land as well. People ought to act according to the balance of that scale.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: But I understand your point of view. Perhaps you would say the laws set by the lords ameer and padishahs are of abnormal balance, and one should act as one's heart dictates.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: However... I dare not trust myself, Narantuya.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: If the day does come when I'm caught by the lords ameer and they give me some ridiculous death sentence, will you feel sorry for me?

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Hah. That's all I need. Looks like you think my death would be a great loss for all Sargon too.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Your help in my grand project would significantly lessen the risk of us failing midway. But I understand if you don't want to.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: People come and go. I'd love to have everyone join me and stay by my side, but if I care too much about those who leave, aren't I just as stupid as the ones who resent me?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What I mean is... let's not make it difficult for each other.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: ...Very well.

steps.name: Aspasia
steps.text: I consider your debt settled.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You're injured.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I'm fine, it's just a scratch...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: You should see to it. I've met many a warrior who lost his life after neglecting a minor injury.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Times have changed... I'll tell you all about modern medical science someday.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Are you going to rest?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: No... I need to tidy up these soaked notes first...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Soaked?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It's a super long story, and I don't know if I'm sane enough right now to tell you the whole thing.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Before we parted this morning, you promised to share the information you obtained with me. Stay true to your word, Pepe.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: ...Okay, I found absolutely nothing today.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I made an announcement, and lots of people came to see me with similar-looking gems, but they were all useless stones.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I spent the whole day watching gem after gem fly past my eyes until my head was spinning. Then I went to get a drink and take a break, but the two kids next to me suddenly started fighting.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: They knocked over the table and my drink, spilling it onto my notebook, and that's how I got this bruise...

spans.text: my drink, spilling it onto my notebook, and that's how I got this bruise...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: That's all I have to share with you, Zubayr.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Got the information you needed from that?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Do you... wish to hear what I experienced today?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Zubayr...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Many strange people came... though they were rather amusing as well.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Let's pick this back up tomorrow. You don't need to sleep, but I'm exhausted.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Pepe... I do not wish to stay inside the museum.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Just bear with it for a few more days... we need to help Titi with her exhibition until its over. That's how we got the gem from her, after all.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Once the exhibition is over, I'll take you to look for the other gemstones.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I do not want to look for gemstones either...

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: What's wrong, Zubayr? As the guardian of the Shah's treasury, aren't you supposed to recover all your memories and resume your original duties?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Are you not the one more eager to locate the treasury?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Ah... yeah, you're right. I mean why else did you think I woke you up?

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Pepe. I am already awake, and you can no longer treat me as a mere artifact. My thoughts and actions are my own to control.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I do not wish to recall all my memories so soon. At least for the moment.

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: Tomorrow we will have fine weather, and I wish to take a walk outside, free of all worry.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: People are going to freak out if they see a museum exhibit getting some sun all alone on the streets!

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: I already told you, I am not an exhibiting artifact!

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: I'm sorry, Zubayr...

steps.name: Zubayr
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: It's already so late though, and I'm REALLY tired, so... we can talk tomorrow, okay?

steps.name: Pepe
steps.text: Good night.
In the empty room, Zubayr tries to press the wall switch and turns the light off.
After a moment, he tries again, and the light comes back on.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Meow?
Mio stands in the middle of a night-shrouded street, staring at a window in the distance with a light repeatedly flickering on and off.
And then—
The light stops flickering, and glass shatters.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Once the south wind passes, it'll be the drought season over there.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Will I manage to make enough money before then?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Alright, prepare to jump...

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: Whoa!

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: Girls are really something these days... What are you doing? Throwing your life away?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What, isn't this normal for the Flood Festival?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I want to ask the river god some questions.

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: Not by jumping into the river though...

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: Also, which history book did you even learn this custom from, girlie?

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: The ancients did ask the river for answers when they were unsure of something, but later, they realized many problems could be solved with money...

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Thanks, but that life hack won't work for me.

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: I can answer your question, though.
The lamplighter raises his lamp and approaches Narantuya.

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: Before the southern wind blows through, you won't have enough money to satisfy your own desires, but it will be what you need.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...I'll rephrase my question and be more specific: where should I go to look for the money?

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: To the depths of the sands.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: This is Sargon, that doesn't do much to narrow it down.

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: I can only answer one more question.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I thought the people of Menat-Ha'mait were generous sorts with unlimited samples to offer?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: No... wait, that's not the question I wanted to ask.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I want to know... will that rigid Minoan come looking for me?

steps.name: Lamplighter
steps.text: Yes.
As soon as the lamplighter finishes, Narantuya catches a glimpse of a shadow on the edge of her vision.
The figure stops in the empty street and looks at her for a moment before turning and leaving.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...Aspasia?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Aspasia!
The shadow crosses the street, and the crimson Kuranta chases after it.
Narantuya can only hear the sound of the wind, the rush of the river, and a song from the lamplighter that gradually fades into silence.

a.text: ♪May I see Him by the waterside, may I follow Him to eternity♪

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...I lost sight of her?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I, Narantuya, actually lost track of a target? Must have been a ghost.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: ...*sigh*.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Forget it, I'm not stupid.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Everyone here is always praying to see a spirit or two, and I heard no footsteps earlier.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: So, this only means I really did see a ghost, yes?
She sits down on the curb.
On the other side of a flowerbed sits someone listening to the river silently in the dark.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: The benches by the river tend to get wet, you might want to wipe it dry first.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: You're not actually scared of ghosts, are you?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What, did you see that shadow too? Did it spook you? Need me to protect you?

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: ...I'm feeling nostalgic.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: I didn't get a good look, but I'm certain it felt like the soul of a late friend or kin.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Two spotting a ghost is always better than just one.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I hear anyone who spots that shadow will receive the blessing of Menat-Ha'mait, but it looks like the two of us here are down on luck.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: ...I merely got into an argument.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What a coincidence. I'm guessing you didn't win?

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: I would not be sitting here if I did.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Haha.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: You know what? Somebody told me ten minutes ago that the locals are never troubled because money can always solve their problems.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I thought that made sense. What's there to be sad about, if you're not as desitute as me?

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: Today, someone threw something at me, another soiled the new cape I got last week, and I was inexplicably married twenty times to people of all genders and ages.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: No one was interested in listening to me either.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: O-Oh... that's pretty unlucky.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: How old are you? They stole your identity for a marriage registration?

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: ...What?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Your voice is a little strange, but you sound young. No offense.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: *sigh* I think I was pretty lucky, when I was around your age.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: One time, we were herding some stolen burdenbeasts back home, and the sky suddenly turned dark. Our headscarves couldn't shield us from the sand flying our way.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: But we had plenty of manpower, and quickly found a somewhat different area to dig into.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Guess what we found? Two houses buried in the sand, just enough to fit everyone. Even came with beds and tables.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: ...Common furnishing you find in ancient tombs.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Hahaha! You know your stuff! I only found out a few years later.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Those were wonderful days.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: Indeed... Time can alter how rivers flow, establish and eradicate cities, bleach bones with the sun, elongate and intensify history.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: It makes one miss the past, and nostalgia... can be a fearsome thing.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Yeah. Miss the past all you want, but you're never getting it back.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: How are the people you've been missing?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: They're alive, but more surviving than living.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: The worst part is that they can't just move on. You have no idea how many of them sold off their blades.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: So as their boss, I owe them.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: I mean, I just need to build a new pile of gold, and those stooges will cheer up and return to the way they used to be.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: I hope that is the case.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: I... don't know either.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: It's like how people risk their lives to catch a glimpse of the river god, but all they end up seeing is the last face they would ever want to see. Is that not a terrifying prospect?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: It's not that scary, if people still choose to chase that mirage.

spans.text: scary, if people still choose to chase that mirage.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Well, that's what my mother always told me, back home:

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: 'We Nightzmora must be the masters of fear, and will never be dominated by it.' That's what they all say.

steps.name: Lost Passerby?
steps.text: —You're a Nightzmora?

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Yeah, why—
Narantuya feels a pat on her shoulder and turns her head on reflex.
She sees no one but the silent street, with its lamps being lit one by one from a distance.
The lamplighter hums a tune as he walks up to them, climbing up a ladder and opening the glass shade to light it.

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: AAAAAAAAHHHHHHH!!!

steps.name: Narantuya
steps.text: Help, HELP! There's a dead guy haunting meee!!!
